findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:6-7 (`push: branches: [main]`); .github/workflows/pr-profile.yml:19-27 (pull_request_target opened/synchronize/reopened, merge_group) with `lake exe cache get` at pr-profile.yml:319 and :419.
findings.fix: State the actual boundary: ci.yml is included because it is the sole publisher, pr-build.yml as the highest-volume consumer; pr-profile.yml has comparable per-PR volume and is deliberately left out as a rollout control.
findings.issue: "limiting the change to the two highest-volume build paths" is inaccurate: ci.yml runs only on main pushes, while the excluded pr-profile.yml runs on every pull_request_target/merge_group event and fetches Mathlib (twice on a pin bump). The reader is told the remaining traffic is negligible when a per-PR path is still uncovered.

findings.evidence: action.yml:28 `path: ${{ env.MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR }}/*.ltar`; grep shows it is set only in .github/workflows/ci.yml:30 and .github/workflows/pr-build.yml:64, and it is not mentioned in the action's inputs or description.
findings.fix: Document the required `MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR` env contract in the action `description` (or the step comment), or make it an explicit required input.
findings.issue: The action's documented interface is only `project-dir`, but it also requires the caller to set `MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR` in the job env (used unguarded in `path`). A future caller — e.g. the pages.yml/pr-profile.yml extension the doc anticipates — that copies the documented usage gets `path: /*.ltar` and a silently useless cache.

summary: The prior two findings are fixed, but the doc justifies the rollout boundary with an inaccurate volume claim (pr-profile.yml fetches Mathlib on every PR, more often than the included main-only ci.yml), and the new composite action documents only project-dir while silently requiring a caller-set MATHLIB_CACHE_DIR.
